items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the highway law, in relation to state liability for defects in
highways
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5422

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the highway law, in relation to state
liability for defects in highways

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill expands the state's liability for damages suffered by individ-
uals due to defects in state highways when the state has actual or
constructive notice of such defects.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends section 58 of the state highway law to
provide that the state shall be liable for damages suffered by any
person for defects in state highways maintained by the state under such
system as the commissioner of transportation may adopt pursuant to
section twelve to of this chapter, providing the state has received
actual or constructive notice of such defects.

Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under current law, Motorists who suffer damage due to defects on local
roads may pursue damages against the locality at any time during the
year so long as the municipality had advance notice of the defect. Under
current law, individuals who suffer damages due to defects in state
roads may pursue these damages against the state only if the incident
occurred between May 15 and November 15.

Statewide reports of the poor conditions of state roadways - some with
three-foot wide potholes and other seemingly ongoing defects - highlight
the need to modify this statute and permit motorists to seek damages all
year long.

This bill would allow motorist's to pursue damages from the state for
defects in state roads all year. This bill will continue to exempt the
state from liability where it does not have advance actual or construc-
tive notice. New York State motorists should not have to pay out-of-
pocket for damages caused by a defect in a state highway that should
have been repaired.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017/18: A910 referred to judiciary; same as S8422 (Boyle) referred to
transportation;
2015/16: A425 referred to judiciary; 2014: A9883--A referred to judici-
ary

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply to any cause of
action that accrues on or after such effective date.

summary: Relates to the liability of the state to any person who suffers damage as a result of a defect in a state highway.
title: Relates to state liability for potholes on state highways

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 165
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 5422, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the highway law, in relation to state liability for
      defects in highways"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill would significantly expand the State's liability for damage
done by potholes by removing the current restrictions  on  recovery  for
winter  month  defects.  Currently, a motorist who suffers damage due to
defects on state highways may only recover for damage occurring  between
May  1  and  November  15  of  each year. This, the sponsor notes, is in
contrast to permissible recovery on  local  roads,  which  is  available
year-round provided the locality had advance notice of the defect.

  This  bill has a number of shortcomings. First, the sponsor presents a
false equivalency when comparing the limited recovery on state roads  to
the  year-round recovery on local roads. Local roadways do not withstand
the same volume of traffic and often restrict larger,  heavier  vehicles
from  travel, thereby avoiding the frequency and severity of damage that
occurs on the more heavily traveled state highways.
 
  If enacted, State agencies and authorities could be forced  to  divert
staff from performing snow and ice removal in order to repair defects in
the  midst of hazardous conditions in order to mitigate liability. These
actions would compromise the safety of  the  traveling  public  and  the
safety of state employees who would remedy such defects.
 
  The  bill  fails  to  acknowledge the reason that the liability of the
state for pothole damage was limited to begin with. Hot Mix Asphalt, the
appropriate material used to fill potholes, is a heated  aggregate  that
must  be combined and mixed at specialized facilities.  These facilities
cease production in late fall through early spring.  As  a  result,  the
repair  material  available  during  winter  months  for repairs is Cold
Patch, which is a less durable material intended only for short-duration
temporary repairs. In addition, the surface and air temperatures in  the
winter  months are too cold to allow proper placement and compaction. If
enacted, this bill would require the state to  be  liable  for  potholes
that cannot be repaired in a quality manner using a more permanent meth-
od until such time as the weather becomes warmer.
 
  Finally, this bill if enacted would result in significant costs to the
state.  As  such,  it  is more properly taken up in the context of State
budget negotiations.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
